idiom_name: private-field state + serialized mailbox on the event loop
implementation_notes: JavaScript has no actor runtime, but its execution model supplies most guarantees once state is closed over: each job runs to completion, so a class with private fields, an array of messages and one async drain function processes messages one at a time without locks - the classic actor object becomes class + queue + promise chain. Real isolation and parallelism need worker_threads (or Web Workers): every Worker is its own agent with its own heap, postMessage passes structured-cloned values between them, and SharedArrayBuffer is the deliberate exception. Choose the event-loop form for UI and I/O-bound coordination and the Worker form when a CPU-bound handler must not block everyone else.
pitfalls: An unbounded mailbox array grows silently: the event loop never applies backpressure, so an overwhelmed actor is a memory leak rather than a slow producer.
The actor is only safe while its state is reachable solely through private fields or the closure; exporting the state object, or mutating a message after sending it, reintroduces shared mutability.
postMessage crosses agent boundaries with structured cloning: functions, class methods and proxies cannot cross, and large payloads are copied (or transferred), so message size matters.
If a handler rejects, the drain promise fails and the message is not retried; add an explicit error or supervision policy rather than leaving the rejection unobserved.
A CPU-bound handler blocks the whole event loop for every other actor on it; move it into a Worker.
